clue.text: Rust-marks caused by them decomposing by the river

definitions.text: Rust-marks caused by them decomposing by the river

indicators.note: decomposing breaks a thing down and reforms it, so the letters of the rodents' name plus the river letter are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Stains on riverside metal turn out to be the work of rotting little animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: the letters of RUST-MARKS are the answer's letters plus R for river, so the rodents and the river, broken down, make the stains. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These water-dwelling rodents live along riverbanks, which the whole clue pictures.

clue.text: Ginger-marked ant destroyed vegetable production

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked and rebuilt, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ant with ginger markings has ruined someone's crop of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing vegetables commercially for sale is the business of a horticultural smallholding.

clue.text: Many in the team move furtively

indicators.note: in places the numeral for many inside the word for the team

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a conventional 'many'

explanation.surface: Lots of players in a squad creep about secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge along sideways and stealthily is to slink.

clue.text: Cite harm caused by tortuous word-making

indicators.note: tortuous means twisting, so the letters of the two words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that harm was done by convoluted wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' is a link. RHEMATIC is a rare word meaning relating to the formation of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the formation of words or verbs, from Greek rhema, a word.

clue.text: Giant bird with a golden tail

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, here of golden

explanation.surface: A huge bird sporting a golden tail.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were a race of giants, so the word is a synonym for colossus.

clue.text: Trudged back to die

indicators.note: back means the word for trudged is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to trape (a variant of traipse) is to trudge wearily, so trudged gives traped

explanation.surface: Someone trudged home only to die.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass away is a euphemism for death, as in 'departed this life'.

clue.text: Old English social-workers encountered in German town

indicators.note: in places the word for encountered inside the German town

parts.note: Ems (Bad Ems) is a spa town in Germany
met is the past tense of meet, encountered

explanation.surface: Elderly English social workers met up in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social-workers' are ants, social insects that work; emmet is an old and dialect English word for an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are social insects famed for labour, and the archaic English name for them is the one wanted.

clue.text: Professional lady shares out pie

indicators.note: printer's pie is jumbled type, so pie signals that the letters of shares out are mixed up

explanation.surface: A professional woman divides up a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like the thing being shared, but in printing 'pie' is type in a jumble, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who writes books for a living is a female writer, a professional lady of letters.

clue.text: Play with boy and side with wild cousin

parts.note: Titus is a boy's name
taken as written
R, for right, is one side

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of cousin run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A drama featuring a lad, a team and an unruly relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'with's are links. ONICUS is the anagram of COUSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's bloodiest tragedy, an early Roman play, is the title meant.

clue.text: Sets off to time the workmen

parts.note: riggers are workmen who fit rigging or scaffolding

explanation.surface: Gets workmen started at the appointed hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate or set something going is a verb sense for starting off an alarm or reaction.

clue.text: Dog star? No, could be the sun

definitions.meaning: a breed of gundog with a rich chestnut coat, the Irish breed

definitions.text: star? No, could be the sun
definitions.meaning: the sun going down glowing crimson at dusk, a ruddy body sinking

explanation.surface: Is the Dog Star the one in question? No, it might be the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog star' points at Sirius, but the dog is one sense and the sun sinking red at evening the other.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the chestnut Irish gundog; the other reads the phrase literally as a crimson sun going down.

clue.text: Became acquainted with Holy Writ inside, hence the composition

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation for Holy Writ within the word for became acquainted

parts.note: met means became acquainted with someone
OT, the Old Testament, is part of Holy Writ

explanation.surface: Getting to know scripture leads to writing a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A short choral piece, usually sacred and unaccompanied, is a musical work.

clue.text: Flushing required English name for treatment

indicators.note: something given treatment is worked over and reshaped, so the letters of name are reordered

explanation.surface: A medical note: flushing is needed, with the English name for the cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' is a link. NEMA is the anagram of NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical procedure washes out the bowel with injected fluid, a flushing of the rectum.

clue.text: Denials of Antigone's metamorphosis

indicators.note: metamorphosis is a change of form, so the letters of the Greek heroine's name, with its s, change shape

explanation.surface: A play asks whether Antigone's transformation amounted to refusals.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of 'Antigone's' does supply an S to the fodder. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Statements saying no are refusals or contradictions, the plural noun of saying not.

clue.text: ANile gull's teasing the water-hens

indicators.note: teasing pulls fibres apart and rearranges them, so the letters of the first words are teased into a new order

explanation.surface: A gull on the Nile pesters the moorhens.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s supplies the final S of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: These marsh birds of the rail family include the moorhen, also called water-hen.

clue.text: From first light Pam stops out — beside these standards

indicators.note: From first takes the opening letter of light
out means disordered, so the letters of Pam stops are put in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: At dawn Pam stops outdoors beside these posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside these' is a link. AMPPOSTS is the anagram of PAM STOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Street lights stand on upright poles, and a standard is a supporting upright pole.

clue.text: Acceptable to be forcing one's way in? It's revolting!

parts.note: U means upper-class and so socially acceptable
prising is levering something open to get inside

explanation.surface: Is it okay to barge in? It's disgusting!
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgusting but means rising in revolt. U for acceptable is the old upper-class usage. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular revolt or rebellion is a rising against authority, hence a revolting.

clue.text: Like mustard?

parts.note: points to the idiom for eagerness that compares an enthusiast to the condiment's sharpness

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as ___ as mustard' means very eager, and the word also means sharp-tasting.

clue.text: No longer an animal I use for food

parts.note: past means over, no longer happening
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An animal no longer kept: I use it for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiced smoked beef is a deli meat, a foodstuff.

clue.text: More than a day's work for the builders

definitions.text: More than a day's work for the builders

parts.words: More than a day's work for the builders
parts.note: alludes to the proverb that a certain Italian capital was not built in a single day

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the Italian capital took longer than one day to construct.

clue.text: He's gone beyond the pale, the sinner

definitions.meaning: someone who has crossed a boundary on to land where he has no right to be
one who transgresses, as in the Lord's Prayer's forgiving of those who wrong us

explanation.surface: An outcast who has gone too far, a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person on land illegally; the other is the biblical wrongdoer of the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Dock a point? That's harsh

parts.note: to dock is to cut off, to sever
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Taking off a point: that's a tough penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern, strict and unsparing are synonyms of harsh.

clue.text: Put into words and sent off speedily

definitions.meaning: dispatched by fast delivery, as a letter by special post

explanation.surface: Said it and posted it fast.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is stated in speech; the other is a parcel sent by fast post.

clue.text: Does wrong —— dunderhead was given a drug

indicators.note: wrong means incorrectly arranged, so the letters of does are put out of order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of dunder is D

explanation.surface: A fool behaving badly was sedated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given a measured amount of medicine has been medicated.

clue.text: Rear coaches

definitions.meaning: to rear is to bring up and educate, a verb
a set of linked railway carriages

explanation.definitionFit: To bring up and teach is one sense; a line of railway carriages is the other.

clue.text: The English point of view?

definitions.meaning: a member of the Germanic tribe from which England takes its name
a slant or perspective on a subject

explanation.surface: Asks what the English perspective on a question might be.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a Germanic settler of England; the other is a slant or perspective.

clue.text: I take the head and cook uses the rest for the children

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so the letters of uses are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: I sit at the top of the table while the cook feeds the rest to the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the head and' and 'the rest for' are links saying I comes first. SSUE is the anagram of USES.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring or progeny are a person's descendants, legally termed this.

clue.text: Longing to be home, clings to doctor

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: the printed words give eight of the fodder letters; the setter's fodder needs an A as well, which the clue as printed omits

explanation.surface: Homesick, someone clutches at the physician.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue lacks an A: CLINGS TO gives eight of the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful yearning for the past or for one's homeland is homesickness.

clue.text: Let in drunken guests

indicators.note: drunken means reeling and unsteady, so the letters of guests stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Tipsy visitors are admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular piece of fabric inserted into a garment is something sewn in.

clue.text: Worshippers upset -—married on 'Sunday!

indicators.note: upset means overturned and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Churchgoers are disturbed by a wedding on the Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted fans or followers who adore someone are worshippers.
